semantics.kv_skap_vault: Maintains the verifier for the user and is the sole source of user-verification state.
semantics.stegos_device: An interchangeable StegOS transport node that may carry or execute bounded work. Device identity, node identity, transport channel identity, local key possession, and local hardware do not establish user-verifier authority and are not verification gates.
semantics.node_local_capability: A node may expose and invoke locally available capabilities after applicable KV/SKAP-backed user-verification state and Interlock/InTr admission are bound to the exact operation. Local execution does not make the node the user verifier.
semantics.transport_integrity: A transport may preserve integrity, freshness, routing, replay protection, and evidence bindings without becoming a user verifier or trust root for the user.
semantics.execution_surface_observation: Connector or runtime observations such as reachable, connected, alive, local, or unavailable describe execution-surface availability only. They never mean authorized, verified, trusted, user-verified, authority-bearing, substrate-unsuitable, or external-device-required.
semantics.device_interchangeability: Replacing one eligible StegOS device/node with another does not change the user's verifier. Only available local capability endpoints and resulting execution evidence may change.
semantics.remote_computer_transport: Remote Computer is a transport/discovery surface only. Capacity discovered through it may execute only after materializing as the canonical StegBrowser/StegOS node class and being admitted as ADMITTED-EPHEMERAL-STEGOS-NODE through Interlock/InTr.
semantics.ephemeral_substrate: Temporary compute is not a separate authority or durable machine dependency. Presence or connectivity grants no execution, transition, WorkerCoordinator claim/fence, credential, custody, publication, or completion authority.
semantics.runtime_substrate_order: Runtime-capable tasks must evaluate the canonical single-device-first substrate order before any remote/external-device last resort. EVIDENCE_REACHABILITY may remain pending but cannot establish UNSUITABLE or create an external-device requirement.
semantics.organization_runtime_reality: Runtime reality for an organization is the organization ledger root: the append-only hash-linked organization receipt chain written under the organization ledger lock by manifest-directed append. A transition within the organization is real when it is appended there. Shipping, releasing, recording or reconstructing it downstream preserves and verifies that reality; it does not constitute it.
semantics.master_records_batch_recording: Master Records records organization batches the organization has independently verified and released, for durable cross-organization custody and complex reconstruction. Its release predecessor is a verified organization receipt-chain segment. It holds no transition, execution, credential, routing or runtime-reality authority, is not a gate on an organization's runtime reality, and is never awaited by a transition. An unreleased or unrecorded batch is a value in the attempted transition's evidence state, not a blocker and not proof of non-occurrence.
semantics.actions_by_manifest: Every action is a manifest-bound attempted state transition. The manifest determines the destination; so long as the destination exists, the transition succeeds at ingress into the Interlock and at egress. Destination liveness, receiver availability, an always-on listener, an external machine, a second user-operated device and a post-closure authentic observer are all prohibited as transition predicates. An unavailable receiver is answered by DURABLE_QUEUE_OR_EVENT_EPHEMERAL_MATERIALIZATION, never by waiting. A surface that cannot yet satisfy this standard must hold a registered exemption carrying an actionable non-ALLOW disposition; silent non-conformance is prohibited.
semantics.completion_evidence_class: Every affirmative completion statement must identify the exact evidence class proven. Source implementation, merge, CI validation, sandbox runtime observation, external/provider observation, Master Records reconstruction, and end-to-end completion are distinct states and may not be collapsed.
semantics.completion_promotion: A stronger evidence class may be asserted only from evidence native to that class. Lower classes never imply higher classes. User-facing unqualified complete/completed is prohibited unless the declared terminal evidence class is satisfied.
semantics.legacy_completion: Historical unqualified completion claims remain provenance only. Without contract v1, an explicit evidence class, and evidence references they cannot satisfy a current terminal predicate, promote task state, or support user-facing complete/completed language.
semantics.connected_device_inventory: Ordinary StegVerse task progression MUST NOT query, inspect, depend on, or report connected-device inventory. Connector/device inventory is outside the runtime dependency model and cannot be used as a blocker, completion gate, execution-surface prerequisite, fallback condition, manual-work requirement, or reason to stop progression. The only exception is a task whose explicit subject is connector/device-inventory management itself.
semantics.zero_connected_devices: Zero connected devices has no StegVerse task-state meaning. It must not be checked for ordinary runtime tasks and, if incidentally known, must be ignored for task progression.
